extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, research administrators, and grant applicants reviewing historical/project award listings
extracted.subtask_description: A compiled listing of funded mathematical-sciences research projects (PI, institution, project title/topic, program code), showing award amounts and durations; useful for understanding what kinds of projects received support. The page is a historical catalog of Scientific Research Project Support entries across many U.S. institutions and subfields of mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program / funding category
rubrics_metrics.description: Header grouping identifying the funding program (e.g., 'SCIENTIHC RESEARCH PROJECT SUPPORT').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page groups entries under the program title; use this to interpret that listed items are awards under that specific program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator (PI) name
rubrics_metrics.description: The named investigator(s) leading the project (examples: 'LEHNER, JOSEPH', 'GREENSPAN, HARVEY P').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI names appear at the start of each entry, often followed by a semicolon and the project title; multiple investigators may be listed with 'AND' or commas. Use PI to identify project leadership and contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The university or institution associated with the PI (examples: 'BOSTON COLLEGE', 'MASSACHUSETTS INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution headings appear as blocks (all-caps) and group subsequent project entries; indicates host organization for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project title / research topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Short title or topic describing the project (examples: 'ASYk'PTOTIC APPROXIMATIOSS', 'AUTOMORPHIC FORMS ASD THE ISDEI THEOREM', 'REGIONAL COSFERESCE ON ANALYSIS ON LIE GROUPS AND HOMOGENEOUS SPACES').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Titles often indicate subfield and scope (research, conference, symposium). They are the primary descriptor of the work being funded—useful for classification by subject area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project type (research, symposium, regional conference, seminar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation within the title that indicates the activity type, e.g., 'SYMPOSIUM', 'REGIONAL CONFERENCE', 'RESEARCH SEMINAR', or plain research topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project-type labels identify whether funds support conferences/symposia or investigator research; examples include 'REGIONAL CONFERENCE', 'SYMPOSIUM', and explicit research-topic titles without those qualifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program/classification code
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenthetical project/program code following the title (examples: '(POiS5i OOl)', '(PCS4iO0i)', '(POi9HS 00i)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These codes appear after project titles and can be used to map entries to internal program classifications or budget/accounting categories; preserve exact code strings when cross-referencing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of the award expressed in months (examples: '12 MONTHS', '18 MONTHS', '6 MONTHS', '24 MONTHS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration is listed for each entry; use it to infer project timescale and to compare typical award lengths across project types or fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount (dollars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Monetary value assigned to the award (examples: '$8,000', '$320,000', '$14,900').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts follow the duration in each entry. They represent the funding level for the stated period and are essential for analyzing funding magnitude by field, institution, or project type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple investigators / co-PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries that list more than one investigator (examples: 'CARRIER, GEORGE P. AND BODUNSKY, BERNARD', 'RAYMOND, FRANK; ...' where joint PIs are separated by 'AND' or commas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of multiple named investigators indicates collaborative projects; capture co-PI relationships to analyze team-based awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject area / subfield identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific mathematics subfield indicated by title words (examples: 'ALGEBRAIC GEOMETRY', 'PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS', 'DIFFERENTIAL EQUATIONS', 'TOPOLOGY', 'NUMERICAL ANALYSIS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subfield phrases within titles enable categorization and topical analysis of funded research; extract exact wording to preserve nuance (e.g., 'FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS' vs 'FUNCTION AVOEBRAS').

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic / scale indicator in title
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, titles include geographic or scope qualifiers such as 'REGIONAL' or 'SUMMER INSTITUTE' (examples: 'REGIONAL CONFERENCE', 'SUMMER INSTITUTE ON HARMONIC ANALYSIS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These qualifiers indicate scale and intended audience for events (local/regional vs national/international) and help distinguish types of conference support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting/presentation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Page presentation conventions: entries list 'PI; PROJECT TITLE (CODE); [duration] MONTHS $[amount]'; institution names in all caps separate blocks of entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding the consistent layout helps automated parsing: expect PI name, semicolon, uppercase title, parenthetical code, duration string, and dollar amount; institutions serve as section headers.
